commands.name: addon-import-get
commands.description: The addon import string for an upcoming raid: who goes by the comp, with their groups, ready to paste into the Vintage addon. The same string the coordinator posts to the officer channel after lock.

commands.name: agent-ask
commands.description: Ask the guild agent a question in plain words ("am I on the roster Thursday?", "who has not answered?"). It answers with the commands you can run; anything that would change data comes back as a confirmation you press. Answers arrive a few seconds later: read them with agent-run-get. Pass `thread` (a channel or chat id) to keep follow-ups in one conversation.

commands.name: agent-config-set
commands.description: Change the guild agent: the model and reasoning effort for questions, and the caps (questions per member per day, questions and Decisions calls per guild per month). Fields left out stay as they are.

commands.name: agent-confirm
commands.description: Run a change the agent prepared for you: the exact command and input it showed. Only the member who asked can confirm, within 5 minutes for destructive changes and 30 for others.

commands.name: agent-decline
commands.description: Drop a change the agent prepared for you, without running it.

commands.name: agent-pause
commands.description: Stop the guild agent: no questions, no wording, no Decisions calls until resumed. Everything falls back to templates and plain commands.

commands.name: agent-resume
commands.description: Turn the guild agent back on after agent-pause.

commands.name: agent-run-get
commands.description: One agent run: its status, the answer once there is one, and any changes waiting for you to confirm. Your own runs; officers see anyone's.

commands.name: agent-runs
commands.description: The agent ledger, newest first: questions, wording jobs, and Decisions calls, with the commands each ran. Members see their own; officers see everyone and can filter by member or kind.

commands.name: agent-status
commands.description: Whether the guild agent is on, its model and caps, and how much it has been used today and this month (questions, wording jobs, Decisions calls, failures in the last day).

commands.name: application-config-get
commands.description: Where new applications are posted, and the onboarding note accepted applicants get.

commands.name: application-config-set
commands.description: Set the recruitment channel new applications are posted to (a Discord channel id, or null to stop posting) and the onboarding note (`{site}` becomes the website address). The channel must be visible to officers only: posts carry each applicant’s answers and labels.

commands.name: application-decline
commands.description: Decline an application, optionally with a reply the applicant gets in a DM. Shows the application first; confirm to decline.

commands.name: application-get
commands.description: Your latest application and where it stands (no id), or one application by id. Officers see the whole application with its labels; applicants see their own status and the reply.

commands.name: application-list
commands.description: Applications, newest first, with their labels (what the text reads as, whether it is complete, fit to the open roles). Filter by status.

commands.name: application-review
commands.description: Answer an application: move it to in-review or accept it, optionally with a reply the applicant gets in a DM. Accepting sends them the onboarding note and asks an officer, in the recruitment channel, to give them the recruit role in Discord.

commands.name: application-submit
commands.description: Apply to raid with Vintage as a raider or flex raider: your character, what you play, a few words about you, your raiding experience, and when you can raid. Needs a Discord account (apply from Discord, or sign in with Discord on the site). Officers answer in Discord.

commands.name: application-withdraw
commands.description: Take back your open application.

commands.name: character-add
commands.description: Register one of your characters (main or alt).

commands.name: character-list
commands.description: Characters for a member (yours by default), or the whole guild for recruits and up.

commands.name: character-remove
commands.description: Remove a character. Shows a preview first; confirm to delete.

commands.name: character-update
commands.description: Change a character’s spec or make it your main.

commands.name: comp-suggest
commands.description: Suggest a raid comp from the signups: who plays, who sits, and what the raid is missing ("need 1 healer", "no Mark of the Wild"), each with a reason.

commands.name: coordinator-config-set
commands.description: Set where the coordinator posts (signup and officer channels), whose answers it chases (expectedRanks), whether it DMs non-responders, whether it posts the weekly roster and recruitment check (weeklyAssessment), and whether each posted raid also gets a Discord server event (serverEvents; the bot needs the Create Events permission).

commands.name: coordinator-log
commands.description: What the coordinator did for a raid and why: posts, reminders, DMs, locks. Answers 'why did the bot ping me?'.

commands.name: coordinator-pause
commands.description: Stop the coordinator: no posts, reminders, or locks until coordinator-resume.

commands.name: coordinator-repost
commands.description: Replace a raid's signup post with a fresh one (the old message is deleted). Use it after the post was deleted or its layout changed.

commands.name: coordinator-resume
commands.description: Restart a paused coordinator. Anything that came due while paused goes out on the next tick.

commands.name: coordinator-run
commands.description: Run a coordinator tick now instead of waiting for the schedule (it runs every few minutes). Safe to repeat: nothing is sent twice.

commands.name: coordinator-status
commands.description: Whether the coordinator is running, its settings, and for each upcoming raid what it has done, what it will do next, and who among the expected ranks has not answered.

commands.name: guild-profile-get
commands.description: The guild’s own words on the public pages: the hero’s pills (ruleset, raid nights, sizes, style) and intro, the About page’s lead and sections, the public Discord invite, and the contact email for privacy and terms questions. `updatedAt` is null while it shows the starter text no officer has saved.

commands.name: guild-profile-set
commands.description: Change the guild profile the public pages show. Give any of: `pills` (short hero facts, in order), `intro` (the hero paragraph), `aboutLead`, `aboutSections` (the whole list of {heading, body}; separate paragraphs in a body with a blank line), `discordInvite` (a discord.gg or discord.com/invite link, or null to remove it), `contactEmail` (or null). What you leave out stays as it is. Answers the profile as it now reads.

commands.name: guild-roles-get
commands.description: The Discord role id → guild rank map that member-sync uses to set rank and tier.

commands.name: guild-roles-set
commands.description: Replace the Discord role id → guild rank map. Shows the diff first; confirm to save. Tiers follow at the next role sync.

commands.name: help-get
commands.description: How to use Random, the guild’s Discord bot: an overview, or one topic’s commands, options, and examples, for your own rank.

topic.description: One topic; leave out for the overview

commands.name: insights-get
commands.description: One run’s findings (the latest without an id). Officers see every raider’s; members see only their own.

commands.name: insights-optin-set
commands.description: Whether you get a private Discord note after a raid with what the log says you could do better. Off until you turn it on.

commands.name: insights-runs
commands.description: Imported runs, newest first: zone, when, how long, who was there.

commands.name: insights-send
commands.description: Send a run’s notes to the raiders who opted in: one private DM each, at most two findings, worded by the agent when it is on. Shows who would get one first; confirm to send. Each run sends once.

commands.name: kill-record
commands.description: Record a boss kill: the raid, the boss (ids from progress-get), when (defaults to now), and what dropped with its quality. The guild’s first kill of a boss is what the ledger shows; later kills are kept as the kill log.

commands.name: member-list
commands.description: Guild members with their rank, tier, and main character. Discord-only friends are not listed.

commands.name: member-me
commands.description: Your member profile: guild rank, tier, Discord roles, preferences, and characters.

commands.name: member-prefs-set
commands.description: Update your preferences: DM opt-out, default character, timezone.

commands.name: member-sync
commands.description: Sync one member's guild rank and tier from their Discord server membership and roles.

commands.name: poll-cancel
commands.description: Cancel a draft or open poll with no result. Votes are kept for history. Shows a preview first; confirm to cancel. Raid leaders only.

commands.name: poll-close
commands.description: Close an open poll now and record its result. Shows the result that would be recorded first; confirm to close. The creator or a raid leader. Closing cannot be undone.

commands.name: poll-create
commands.description: Create a poll: a question, 2–25 options, a method (single, multi, or ranked), who may vote (eligibleTier, raider by default), and optional anonymity, hidden results, quorum, and close time. Opens at once unless open is false or opensAt is later. Raiders create polls for raiders and up; reaching members or recruits takes a raid leader, and nobody can target a tier above their own.

commands.name: poll-get
commands.description: One poll, your own vote, and the ballot count. The tally is included when you may see it (per the poll’s resultsVisible; officers always).

commands.name: poll-list
commands.description: Polls you may vote on, soonest to close first. Filter by status (open by default) or tag. Each includes the ballot count; tallies are left to poll-get and poll-results.

commands.name: poll-open
commands.description: Open a draft poll for voting now. The creator or a raid leader.

commands.name: poll-results
commands.description: The tally for a poll, and who voted for what when the poll is not anonymous. Live results show only when the poll allows it; officers always see the tally but never the voters of an anonymous poll.

commands.name: poll-sweep
commands.description: Open drafts whose opensAt has passed and close open polls whose closesAt has passed. Safe to run repeatedly; the cron runs it every few minutes.

commands.name: poll-update
commands.description: Change a draft or open poll: question, description, close time, result visibility, quorum, or tags. Options can change only while nobody has voted. The creator or a raid leader.

commands.name: progress-get
commands.description: The progression ledger: the three launch raids, every boss with the guild’s first-kill time (null until it dies), the next target per raid, the totals, and the latest first kill with its loot. Before the raids unlock, `open` is false and every slot is empty. Boss names flagged `datamined` come from the beta client, not from Blizzard.

commands.name: raid-cancel
commands.description: Cancel a raid. Shows a preview first; confirm to cancel. Signups stay for history.

commands.name: raid-complete
commands.description: Mark a raid as done after it started. Records attendance (the roster, or accepted signups when no roster was set) and starts post-raid work.

commands.name: raid-create
commands.description: Create a one-off event (not from a schedule), open for signups: a raid (10, 20 or 40), a dungeon (5), a battleground (10, 15 or 40), or another event (1 to 40). roleTargets default to the kind: raid comps by size, 1 tank/1 healer/3 dps for dungeons, no tank for battlegrounds, none for other.

commands.name: raid-get
commands.description: One raid with signup counts and your own signup. Recruits and up see the full signup list.

commands.name: raid-list
commands.description: Raids in a time window, soonest first. Defaults to open and locked raids in the next 14 days.

commands.name: raid-night-poll
commands.description: Ask the raid which night works: post a poll of 2–10 start times for a one-off raid (or another kind: dungeon, battleground, other, with optional roleTargets). When the poll closes, the coordinator creates the event at the winning time; a tie, a missed quorum, or no votes goes to the ops channel instead. Labels use timeZone (New York by default); the post shows each time in every reader’s own zone.

commands.name: raid-reschedule
commands.description: Move a raid to a new start time. Signups and roster are kept.

commands.name: recruiting-get
commands.description: What the website’s recruiting band says: the headline, the pitch, and each class the guild is recruiting with the specs wanted and how much (high, medium, closed). `updatedAt` is null while it still shows the starter text no officer has saved.

commands.name: recruiting-set
commands.description: Change the website’s recruiting band. Give any of: `headline`, `pitch`, and `needs` (the whole list, one row per class (the band sorts high, medium, closed, keeping your order within each): wowClass, specs as free text like "holy · discipline" or "any", need high | medium | closed). What you leave out stays as it is. Answers the band as it now reads.

commands.name: roster-bench
commands.description: Bench a signed-up character for this raid (they keep their signup).

commands.name: roster-lock
commands.description: Lock signups for a raid; after this only raid leaders can change them.

commands.name: roster-move
commands.description: Put a signed-up character in a raid group (1–8 for 40s; 5 per group).

commands.name: roster-remove
commands.description: Remove someone's signup from a raid entirely. Shows a preview first; confirm to remove.

commands.name: roster-unlock
commands.description: Reopen signups for a locked raid.

commands.name: run-import
commands.description: Import one Farsight Crawler run summary (the `farsight.run` v1 upload, never the raw log). Vintage keeps the run, finds what each raider could do better with the evidence, and links characters to members by name. Importing the same run again does nothing.

commands.name: schedule-create
commands.description: Create a recurring raid night, e.g. Molten Core every Tuesday and Thursday at 20:00 New York time, or a weekly dungeon or battleground with kind (default raid). Events are created ahead of time by schedule-materialize.

commands.name: schedule-list
commands.description: List raid schedules (active ones unless includeInactive).

commands.name: schedule-materialize
commands.description: Create the raid events each active schedule needs over its lead window (default 7 days). Safe to run repeatedly: an occurrence that already has an event, even a cancelled one, is skipped.

commands.name: schedule-update
commands.description: Change a schedule (time, days, kind, size, timings, comp targets) or pause it with active: false. Raids already created keep their time; use raid-reschedule for those.

commands.name: signup-get
commands.description: Your signup for a raid. Raid leaders may look up anyone's with memberId.

commands.name: signup-list
commands.description: Everyone signed up for a raid, best answer first (accepted before tentative).

commands.name: signup-set
commands.description: Sign up for a raid with one of your characters, or change your answer (accepted, late, tentative, bench, declined). One signup per member per raid. Raid leaders may sign up anyone's character and may change locked raids.

commands.name: vote-cast
commands.description: Vote on an open poll, or change your vote. choices are option ids: one for single polls, up to maxChoices for multi, and in preference order for ranked. One ballot per member; the same vote from Discord or the website replaces the last one.

commands.name: vote-retract
commands.description: Take back your vote on an open poll.
